candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is Extrapyramidal syndromes of chronic kidney disease and dialysis (EPS-CKDD), a uremia-related metabolic encephalopathy. While the MRS lactate peak and bilateral lenticular nucleus T2 hyperintensity with lentiform fork sign could superficially suggest Leigh syndrome, the clinical context (2-year dialysis history, diabetic nephropathy, subacute onset following GI illness, hyperperfusion on ASL, normal DAT scan with increased accumulation, and no genetic/mitochondrial workup pointing to Leigh) firmly anchors the diagnosis to EPS-CKDD. Leigh syndrome is a distinct genetic mitochondrial disease entity, not a manifestation of CKD/dialysis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Leigh syndrome is a primary mitochondrial disorder typically presenting in infancy/childhood; adult-onset forms exist but are rare genetic conditions unrelated to dialysis/CKD context

case_quality_flags: Lentiform fork sign on T2 MRI is characteristic of uremic encephalopathy/EPS-CKDD; overlap with Leigh syndrome imaging features noted but clinical context is decisive
DAT scan showing increased accumulation (not decreased) argues against primary dopaminergic degeneration and supports metabolic etiology
